# LLMScale

> LLMScale works out how much GPU memory a large language model needs — weights, KV cache, context window and concurrent users — from each model's own architecture, and which GPUs hold it. It runs entirely in the browser, with no account and no backend. Every page also exists in Turkish under https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/tr/.

Every figure comes from one engine. Weights are parameters × bytes per parameter (FP32 4, BF16/FP16 2, FP8/INT8 1, INT4 0.5). The KV cache is 2 × layers × key-value heads × head dimension × bytes × context × concurrent sequences, read from each model's config.json; models with multi-head latent attention (DeepSeek) cache layers × (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) × bytes per token instead. Overhead is a stated share of weights and cache plus a fixed CUDA context. A discrete GPU is budgeted at 95% of its memory; a unified-memory device at the share its GPU can address. Mixture-of-Experts models need memory for every expert but decode through the active ones. The engine is checked against published results: ZeRO's 16 bytes per parameter for mixed-precision Adam, QLoRA fine-tuning a 65B model on one 48 GB GPU, DeepSeek-V2's MLA cache formula, gpt-oss-120b fitting one 80 GB GPU, and MoE model cards' active parameter counts. The figures are for capacity planning; serving engines, paged attention, prefill and sliding-window layers are not modelled.

## Tools

- [LLM VRAM Calculator — Weights, KV Cache & GPU Fit](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/): Estimate the GPU memory an LLM needs: model weights, KV cache, context window and concurrent users — then see which GPUs fit. Pulls live config from Hugging Face.
- [Compare LLMs Side by Side — Specs & Task Fit](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/compare.html): Compare 2–4 Hugging Face LLMs side by side: parameters, context, quantization, capabilities and per-task fit — see which model is better for which use, from live Hugging Face data.
- [Fine-Tuning VRAM Calculator — LoRA, QLoRA & Full](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/train.html): Work out the GPU memory a fine-tune needs: LoRA, QLoRA or full. Gradients, optimizer state and the activations kept for the backward pass, with the GPUs that fit. Validated against the ZeRO and QLoRA papers.
- [LLM 101 — how an LLM works, visualized](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/learn.html): An interactive, animated walkthrough of how a large language model turns a sentence into the next word — tokenization, embeddings, attention, layers and sampling, as a 3D neural constellation.
- [LLM Anatomy — Parameters, Precision & KV Cache](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/anatomy.html): A visual X-ray of any Hugging Face model: where its parameters go (embeddings / attention / experts), its weight size at each precision, architecture, GQA and KV-cache growth — from live Hugging Face data.
- [LLM Name Decoder — 70B, A3B, AWQ, GGUF, FP8](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/decode.html): Decode any LLM model name: what 70B, AWQ, GGUF, FP8, A3B, Instruct and more mean — colour-coded, explained, and interactive.
- [LLM Task Fit — Is This Model Right for the Job?](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/fit.html): Check whether an LLM fits your task — chat, code, RAG, agents, reasoning, vision, embeddings — scored from the model's real size, context, tuning and modality. Live Hugging Face data.
- [vLLM Serve Parameters — Tuned Command Helper](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/vllm.html): Generate a tuned vllm serve command for any model — flags for throughput, latency, accuracy or memory, plus tool-calling, long context and quantization, with a copyable command.

## Concepts

Overview: https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/concepts/

- [GQA, MQA and MLA: Attention and KV Cache Size](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/concepts/gqa-mqa-mla.html): How multi-head, multi-query, grouped-query and multi-head latent attention change an LLM's KV cache, with Llama 3.3 70B Instruct and DeepSeek V3 worked through and 10 models side by side.
- [KV Cache Size: Formula and Examples](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/concepts/kv-cache.html): How big an LLM's KV cache gets: the formula, a worked example with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, per-token figures for popular models, and what concurrency, FP8 and grouped-query attention do to it.
- [LLM Quantization and VRAM: BF16, FP8, INT4](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/concepts/quantization.html): How much GPU memory BF16, FP8, INT8 and INT4 weights take for 8B to 405B models, what AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF, MXFP4 and NF4 are, and why quantizing weights leaves the KV cache as it is.

## Models

Overview: https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/models/

- [DeepSeek V3 VRAM Requirements](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/models/deepseek-v3.html): DeepSeek V3 needs 1403.9 GiB of GPU memory at BF16 and 352.0 GiB at INT4 for one user at 8k context. Memory by precision and context, the GPUs that hold it, concurrent users and fine-tuning memory.
- [Gemma 2 27B IT VRAM Requirements](https://tahircengiz.github.io/LLMScale/models/gemma-2-27b.html): Gemma 2 27B IT needs 59.64 GiB of GPU memory at BF16 and 17.85 GiB at INT4 for one user at 8k context.
